sections.title: The Call of Samuel
observations: In this section, we see God calling Samuel while he is still a boy serving in the temple under Eli. This highlights the theme of God choosing unlikely individuals for His purposes, as Samuel is not yet fully aware of God's voice.
The repetition of Samuel's name emphasizes God's personal call and the importance of listening to Him. It also shows that God is actively involved in the lives of His people, even from a young age.

sections.title: Eli's Role and Recognition
observations: Eli, the priest, plays a crucial role in helping Samuel understand that it is God who is calling him. This reflects the importance of mentorship and guidance in spiritual growth.
Eli's recognition of God's voice also serves as a reminder that spiritual leaders must be attuned to God's communication and be able to guide others accordingly.

sections.title: The Prophecy Against Eli's House
observations: God reveals to Samuel the judgment that is to come upon Eli's household due to the sins of his sons and Eli's failure to restrain them. This serves as a sobering reminder of the consequences of sin and the importance of accountability in leadership.
The prophecy signifies a shift in leadership from Eli's family to Samuel, indicating God's sovereignty in choosing His leaders.

importantVerses.commentary: This verse highlights the moment when Samuel finally responds to God's call, illustrating the importance of being attentive to God's voice.
This verse emphasizes that God was with Samuel and let none of his words fall to the ground, indicating God's approval and the prophetic authority Samuel would carry.

questions: What does Samuel's response to God's call teach us about listening for God's voice in our own lives?
How does Eli's failure to discipline his sons serve as a warning for spiritual leaders today?
In what ways does this chapter illustrate the theme of God's sovereignty in choosing leaders?
